newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-FALCONS ACQUIRE QUARTERBACK CHRIS CHANDLER FROM OILERS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-FALCONS ACQUIRE QUARTERBACK CHRIS CHANDLER FROM OILERS.

text.p: The Atlanta Falcons acquired veteran quarterback Chris Chandler from the Houston Oilers for a pair of 1997 draft choices Monday.

Chandler, who has two years remaining on his contract, immediately steps in as the Falcons' starting quarterback. Atlanta waived starting quarterback Jeff George after suspending him for "conduct detrimental to the team" last October and two of its other quarterbacks -- Bobby Hebert and Billy Joe Tolliver -- are unrestricted free agents.
The desperate circumstances made it a priority for new Falcons coach Dan Reeves to acquire a quarterback.

The departure of Chandler from Houston makes room for Steve McNair to become the Oilers' starter in 1997. Houston succeeded in dumping Chandler's $1.55 million salary figure from the 1997 cap along with acquiring draft picks.
The 31-year-old Chandler started at quarterback the last two years for Houston and completed 409-of-676 passes for 4,559 yards with 33 touchdowns and 21 interceptions.
His 33 touchdown passes in two years with Houston are just eight shy of the 41 he threw during the first seven years of his NFL career with Indianapolis, Tampa Bay, Arizona and the St. Louis Rams.
Chandler threw a career-high 17 touchdown passes in 1995.
